title: 15-Minute Kerala Prawns
intro: Kashmiri chilli paste, ghee, curry leaves, and prawns that stay juicy because you pull them the second they curl.

items: 400 g large prawns, cleaned and deveined
1½ tbsp ginger-garlic paste (or 5–6 garlic cloves + 1 inch ginger, fresh)

method: Cover the dried chillies with hot water and leave to soften.
Drain (keep a little of the water) and blend with the onion, garlic and ginger to a smooth paste, using the soaking water to loosen.
Rub the paste on the prawns, add all four powders and salt. Mix and marinate 15 minutes to an hour.
Heat the ghee in a hot pan and add the curry leaves; let them crackle.
Add the prawns on high heat, stirring. The second they turn pink and curl, take them off the heat. Any longer and they go rubbery.
Add lots of coriander, squeeze over the lemon and give it one toss. Serve with rice, or a cucumber-onion salad to keep it light.
tips: Off the heat the moment they curl. That's the whole recipe.
Fresh ginger and garlic over paste if you've got them. The difference is real.

Vegetarian? Same paste, same spices, with 400 g paneer cubes or 300 g halved mushrooms. Marinate 15 minutes, then into the ghee on high: paneer till the edges catch, mushrooms till the water's gone. Paneer gets you about 18 g protein a serving, nearly the same as the prawns.
